findings.desc: core/proofstory.ts:1326-1367 buildScopeShrinkageDecision: withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs are derived only from the current call args (optionalStringArray(args.x)), never merged with existing.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs. If scope_shrinkage_decision_set is invoked twice under the same decisionId (e.g. withdraw CHK-002 in call 1, then withdraw AB-1 in call 2 without repeating withdrawnChecklistItemRefs), the persisted decision.json silently narrows to only the latest calls refs, so scope_shrinkage_decision_get under-reports the cumulative withdrawal history for that decisionId. The actual checklist item status / proofstory.json bindingDispositions remain correct (stamped durably at write time, not re-derived from this field), and the empty-scope floor still works correctly because it unions the fresh decision with the already-persisted contract.bindingDispositions -- so this is an audit-trail/read-model completeness gap in decision.json, not a gating bypass. Worth a merge-with-existing fix or an explicit doc note that repeat calls under one decisionId must re-supply the full ref set.
findings.resolvedReason: ac756995e7: buildScopeShrinkageDecision now UNIONs withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs/evidenceRefs with existing (unionStringRefs). Regression in scope-shrinkage-withdrawal-floor-smoke (c865b13ba6): two sequential calls under one decisionId accumulate both ref lists.

findings.desc: concept-incompleteness: packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts buildScopeShrinkageDecision (~line 1323) rebuilds withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs/evidenceRefs from args ONLY (optionalStringArray(args.X, ...)), never merged with existing.X. Reproduced: seed a story, call scope_shrinkage_decision_set withdrawing CHK-002 (decision.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs=[CHK-002], decisionId=SD-x) then call it again withdrawing AB-1 only (same decisionId, reused since args.decisionId omitted) -> decision.withdrawnChecklistItemRefs becomes [] even though checklist.json still correctly shows CHK-002 status=withdrawn decisionRef=SD-x. The decision record (the promised single authorizing record both layers cite, CHK-003) becomes a false/incomplete audit trail of what it actually authorized after a second legitimate call under the same decisionId -- contradicting the storys own storage-honesty principle. Compounding: withdrawnChecklistItemIdsFrom (core/proofstory.ts) is imported into handlers/proofstory.ts but never called there, so unlike bindings (withdrawnBindingIdsFrom feeds effectiveAcceptanceBindings), there is no symmetric checklist-side consumer of the decisions own arrays -- only the per-item stamp on checklist.json keeps things functionally correct, so the decision.json array drift is currently latent (no gate breaks) but is a real half-migrated inconsistency in the new vocabulary the story introduced. No smoke test exercises calling scope_shrinkage_decision_set twice under the same decisionId with different ref sets.
findings.resolvedReason: Same root defect as F-001, fixed in ac756995e7 (union-with-existing). Dead withdrawn*IdsFrom imports removed from handlers/proofstory.ts. Two-sequential-call regression added in c865b13ba6 proves accumulation + immutable decisionId.

findings.desc: handlers/proofstory.ts:75-88 normalizeScopeRefArray duplicates core/proofstory.ts:258-267 optionalStringArray (same non-empty-string-array-with-dedup logic, comment even says it mirrors the core helper) instead of exporting and reusing it. Low-severity DRY nit: if the core validation rule ever changes, the handler copy can silently drift out of sync since nothing enforces they stay identical.
findings.resolvedReason: ac756995e7: exported optionalStringArray from core/proofstory.ts, reused it in the handler, deleted the duplicate normalizeScopeRefArray.

findings.desc: CHK-002:edge:0 evidence overclaims: intent names 5 call sites (checklist.ts:82, story-query.ts:568, hints.ts:70, session.ts:435, milestone-status.ts) that must exclude withdrawn from delivered counts. Cited evidence (withdrawn-disposition-smoke.ts) only exercises checklist.ts (checklist_get slim + summarizeChecklist). grep confirms story-query.ts, hints.ts, session.ts, milestone-status.ts are never touched by either smoke task, though git diff shows each carries its OWN independently modified counting/rendering implementation (duplicated, not delegating to checklist.ts summarizeChecklist). Passing the checklist.ts test does not prove correctness for the other 4 named, load-bearing sites; no test anywhere in repo touches them.
findings.resolvedReason: c865b13ba6: withdrawn-disposition-smoke now exercises story_list (checklist 1/2 +1w), hints decorateResult all-terminal advancement, and buildMilestoneStatusReport (withdrawn subObjective terminal, checklist=complete) with a non-terminal CONTROL differential — the previously-untested count consumers are now covered.

findings.desc: concept-incompleteness: packages/main/src/dashboard.ts:111 (checklistDone = cl.items.filter(i => i.status === 'done').length) and the checklistDone/checklistTotal progress bar rendered at dashboard.ts:217-218 were not migrated to isDeliveredChecklistStatus/isTerminalChecklistStatus (core/checklist-status.ts) added by this story. dashboard.ts is outside the storys enumerated ~24 status===done sites / touchpoints (core+handlers only), but it is a real done consumer (the lattice serve Dashboard active-story progress bar). A withdrawn item is correctly excluded from checklistDone (not overcounted as delivered) but checklistTotal still includes it and there is no withdrawn bucket, so a story with a legitimately withdrawn item can never show 100% progress on this bar -- it silently buckets withdrawn as still-outstanding/pending forever, the exact half-migrated pattern CHK-002 was meant to eliminate everywhere.
findings.resolvedReason: ac756995e7: dashboard.ts migrated to isDeliveredChecklistStatus/isWithdrawnChecklistStatus; added checklistWithdrawn bucket; progress bar fills on terminal (done+withdrawn)/total so a withdrawn item reaches 100%, with a dim (+N withdrawn) label.

findings.desc: CHK-002:adversarial:0 evidence overclaims: intent names 4 renderers (checklist_get, story_get, session_brief, exports) that must never print withdrawn as DONE. Cited evidence only asserts checklist_get renders status withdrawn/notEqual done (withdrawn-disposition-smoke.ts lines ~160-163). story_get (story-query.ts), session_brief (session.ts) and any export path are never exercised for this claim in either smoke; grep withdrawn across src confirms zero test touches those renderers. Note textually narrows to just checklist_get while the intent it is bound to names 4 surfaces.
findings.resolvedReason: c865b13ba6: smoke now asserts story_get renders withdrawn (never done) and session_brief (real git-backed root) shows the withdrawn block and never 2/2 done — the additional renderers are covered.

findings.desc: CHK-005:edge:0 second clause overclaims: intent requires citing two different decision ids across the checklist/binding layers for the same shrinkage to be refused. Neither smoke tests this; the evidence note instead argues single-applier design makes cross-layer id mismatch structurally impossible. Code inspection (handlers/proofstory.ts scope_shrinkage_decision_set + core/proofstory.ts buildScopeShrinkageDecision) shows decisionId is an explicit optional override with no check against the existing stored decisionId: a second scope_shrinkage_decision_set call passing an explicit decisionId different from the one already stamped on an earlier withdrawn checklist item would let a new binding withdrawal cite a different decisionRef than the earlier item, and nothing refuses it. This scenario is untested and the structural-impossibility claim in the note does not hold.

CHK-005:adversarial:0 evidence overclaims file/level: note says the smoke calls scope_shrinkage_decision_set on the handler directly and the ref/authority refusals still fire at the handler level, citing withdrawn-disposition-smoke.ts. The ref refusals (bad item/binding) ARE exercised at the handler level in that file (h.ps.scope_shrinkage_decision_set with bad refs). But the authority refusal (userConfirmed missing on a confirmed decision) is never called through ps.scope_shrinkage_decision_set (the handler) in either smoke; it is only exercised by calling the pure buildScopeShrinkageDecision() function directly, and that test lives in the OTHER file (scope-shrinkage-withdrawal-floor-smoke.ts lines ~151-156), not the cited file. The handler also has its own separate defense-in-depth authority check (hasWithdrawals && !(confirmed&&userConfirmed)) that is never exercised at all (e.g. via decision=rejected + withdrawal refs).

CHK-003:happy:0 partial gap: intent requires buildScopeShrinkageDecision to persist evidenceRefs (in addition to decisionId/withdrawnChecklistItemRefs/withdrawnAcceptanceBindingRefs) and scope_shrinkage_decision_get to return them. evidenceRefs is a real optional field on BuildScopeShrinkageDecisionArgs/ScopeShrinkageDecisionData (core/proofstory.ts ~1306,1328,1367) but is never passed as an arg nor asserted in either smoke (grep evidenceRefs across both smoke files: zero hits). The evidence note is honest about what it does test (does not claim evidenceRefs) but the must-intent is only partially covered. Low severity because evidenceRefs is optional audit-only metadata with no gating consumer.
